name: main-write-lock-coverage-guard
title: Close main-write-lock coverage gaps so concurrent sessions cannot race main-branch mutations
description: The shared-main-worktree fleet model means concurrent sessions mutate the same main branch. Any CLI path that commits to or mutates main WITHOUT holding the main-write-lock can be raced by a concurrent session — B-7365 just fixed exactly such a gap (the INIT_CHECK reconcile committed to main + merged without the lock, causing metadata corruption). Lock coverage today is by-convention (CLAUDE.md lists DONE/done_recover/gap_log/audit/story_create/B-META as locked), with no mechanical guard ensuring every main-mutating path is locked, so future code can reintroduce a B-7365-class gap. Scope: (1) audit all CLI paths that commit to / mutate the main branch or main worktree and identify any not under the lock; (2) wrap remaining unlocked main-mutating paths in withReentrantMainWriteLock; (3) add a regression guard (a test that fails if a main-mutating commit path is not under the lock) so future gaps are caught mechanically. NOTE: full physical per-session checkout isolation (the maximalist 'separate worktree per session' architecture) is the larger alternative and is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE here — this story bounds the fix to lock-coverage hardening, which addresses the actual concurrent-mutation corruption risk that the shared-worktree model exposes.
